## Computational Analysis of Visual Social Media · Winter 2026/27

This project-centred research seminar focuses on **frame analysis with vision-language models**. Together, we study political TikTok content with possible AI components. We combine theoretical work on framing with data collection, qualitative exploration, human annotation, and computational experiments.

Taught by [Michael Achmann-Denkler](https://go.ur.de/michael-achmann), Media Informatics, University of Regensburg.

### How We Work

As a seminar, we collect a shared corpus, develop a coding framework from literature and the data, and test it in pilot rounds. We then create independent human annotations and document how a shared reference dataset is derived.

Teams compare models or input representations. Prompts are developed on pilot material; the shared test dataset is reserved for evaluation. Document what evidence supports an item's inclusion in the corpus, including any assessment of AI use. A possible AI component is a sampling criterion to investigate, not an established fact about every collected item.

### Learning Objectives

By the end of the seminar, you should be able to:

- Explain framing and translate theoretical concepts into explicit coding rules.
- Prepare and analyse political videos with vision-language models.
- Compare model outputs with independent human annotations.
- Report findings, uncertainty, and methodological limitations.

## Requirements and Documentation

- Prepare independently: engage with literature, research questions, and operationalisation.
- Contribute regularly to your group and seminar discussions.
- Maintain a shared project document throughout the semester.
- Record sources, data selection, coding rules, model settings, and changes. Keep disagreements and failed attempts visible in the record.
- Explain the study design, present results, and discuss limitations in a final project report.

### Project Report

The working plan is a **joint group report of approximately 20 pages**, organised into Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, with APA citations.

### Use of AI Tools

Follow the course-specific AI rules and the applicable general guidelines provided through the course. Check all submitted content; the team must understand and stand behind it. Disclose the tool or model, its purpose, the affected work steps or parts of the submission, and its specific contribution.
